entities.summary:
British Airways plc is the flag carrier airline of the United Kingdom, founded in 1974 through the merger of British European Airways and British Overseas Airways Corporation. Operating from London Heathrow, the world's busiest international airport, it serves 170+ destinations across 80 countries and is one of the oldest airlines in the world.

British Airways operated Concorde — the world's only commercial supersonic aircraft — from 1976 to 2003, carrying passengers across the Atlantic at Mach 2 in under three and a half hours, a luxury experience that defined a golden age of aviation glamour. The airline's 1987 privatization under Margaret Thatcher's government became a landmark in the global wave of state airline privatizations.

British Airways' parent International Airlines Group (IAG), formed in 2011 with Iberia of Spain, also acquired Vueling and Aer Lingus, creating one of Europe's largest aviation groups. The airline suffered profound crises including the 2008 global financial shock, 2010 strike disruptions, a massive 2018 IT failure, a data breach exposing 500,000 customer records (£20 million GDPR fine), and the catastrophic COVID-19 pandemic causing 12,000 job losses. Its long-haul premium business class remains a benchmark in airline hospitality.
